text: A striking implication of Integrated Information Theory (IIT) for artificial systems is that...
choices: any system that passes the Turing test is thereby conscious
consciousness depends only on behavioral competence, not on architecture
silicon can never realize consciousness under any architecture whatsoever
purely feedforward networks have essentially zero Phi and so are not conscious, however sophisticated their behavior
explanation: On IIT, consciousness is integrated information (Phi), and feedforward networks such as most deep-learning systems have essentially zero Phi regardless of performance, while recurrent systems can have high Phi. IIT concerns intrinsic causal structure, not behavior (against A and B), and it is substrate-neutral, so C mischaracterizes it (that is closer to Searle's biological naturalism).
